title: Pagan confession: we adore visible images unto the honor of the invisible God—Recognitiones and Lactantius
source_text: XLIX. Proinde profitebantur se in suis simulachris invisibilem Deum adorare. Nos, inquiunt, ad honorem invisibilis Dei, imagines visibiles adoramus. Apud authorem Recognitionum, quae Clementi Romano tribuuntur, libro quinto. Et similiter apud Lactantium, Non ipsa, inquiunt, timemus, sed eos ad quorum imaginem facta, & quorum nominibus consecrata sunt. Institutionum libro secundo capite secundo.
pass_a_gloss: Accordingly they professed that in their simulacra they adore the invisible God. We, they say, unto the honor of the invisible God, adore visible images. In the author of the Recognitions, which are attributed to Clement of Rome, book five. And likewise in Lactantius, Not them, they say, do we fear, but those to whose image they were made, and to whose names they were consecrated. Institutions book two chapter two.
pass_b_english: Pagan line in the Clementine Recognitions: visible images for invisible God’s honor.
Lactantius records the same: fear the named gods, not the crafted things.
